text: The following question stood in the name of  Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap –  8  To ask the Minister for Manpower whether the Ministry maintains or plans to set up a watchlist for companies that engage in discriminatory employment practices not related to nationality but to other attributes, such as gender and ethnicity.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: We expect all employers to abide by the principles of fair and merit-based employment practices outlined in the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP) will engage companies on whom we have received complaints or feedback and guide them to improve their employment practices.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: How many companies are currently on the watchlist on discriminatory practices?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And what proportion of those companies on the watchlist are there for nationality-based discriminatory practices, as opposed to suspected discriminatory practices on other dimensions?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: That is an even more direct impact than putting out a watchlist.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We will certainly take every feedback that is surfaced to us, any complaint, we will take it very seriously and investigate very thoroughly.
